panels.title: Node Health — is this node starved, and on what?
Load1 per Core
panels.description: Load average normalised by core count. >1 means the run queue is longer than the machine is wide.

panels.title: CPU Pressure
panels.description: PSI: share of wall time some task was runnable but waiting on CPU.

panels.title: IO Stall (full)
panels.description: PSI: share of wall time *every* task was blocked on IO — the node did no useful work at all.

panels.title: CPU by Mode
panels.description: Stacked to 100% of one core's worth of time, averaged across cores. Watch `iowait` and `system`.

panels.title: Pressure Stall (PSI)
panels.description: The single best 'why is this node slow' signal. 'some' = at least one task stalled; 'full' = everything stalled.

panels.title: Disk Utilisation by Device
panels.description: Fraction of wall time the device had at least one request in flight. Sustained 1.0 = saturated.

panels.title: Disk Average Queue Depth
panels.description: Average number of requests queued. Climbing queue depth with flat throughput = the device is the bottleneck.

options.content:
**Host processes, from process-exporter.** This is the layer cAdvisor cannot reach: `kubelet`, `containerd`, `iscsid`, Longhorn engines, and kernel threads such as `nfsd` and `kswapd`. Processes are grouped by executable name (`comm`), so all `containerd-shim` instances aggregate into one row — usually what you want when asking what the node is spending itself on.

Two caveats. Disk figures come from `/proc/<pid>/io`, so **kernel threads report CPU honestly but near-zero IO bytes** — `nfsd` serving a heavy read shows up as CPU, not bytes. And a container's processes appear here *as well as* in the pod row below, under their program name rather than their pod name; the two rows are different cuts of the same node, not separate workloads.

panels.title: Top Host Processes by CPU
panels.description: CPU cores consumed, user + system.

panels.title: Top Host Processes by Memory (RSS)
panels.description: Resident set size. Proportional (smaps) memory is not collected — see --gather-smaps=false in the DaemonSet.

panels.title: Top Host Processes by Disk Write
panels.description: From /proc/<pid>/io write_bytes: bytes actually sent to the storage layer, not just written to page cache.

panels.title: Top Host Processes by Disk Read
panels.description: From /proc/<pid>/io read_bytes. Reads served from page cache do not appear here.

panels.title: Host Process CPU by Mode
panels.description: Splits the CPU column into user vs system. A process heavy in `system` is spending its time in the kernel — often IO or syscall churn.

panels.title: Host Processes: Threads & Open FDs
panels.description: Runaway thread or descriptor counts usually precede a node problem.

panels.title: Host Process Cost Table (sortable)
panels.description: One row per process group on this node. Click a column header to rank by that resource.

panels.title: Most Expensive Pods on this Node

options.content: **What this row can and cannot see.** These panels come from cAdvisor, so they cover *containers* only — host processes such as `kubelet`, `containerd`, `iscsid`, Longhorn engines and kernel `nfsd` threads are invisible here. Disk figures are **block IO through cgroups**, which means **NFS traffic does not appear**: a pod reading hard from `192.168.50.52` shows near-zero disk here while hoyt's disks saturate. Cross-check the NFS panels below, and the per-device utilisation above, before concluding a pod is idle.

panels.title: Top Pods by CPU
panels.description: CPU cores consumed.

panels.title: Top Pods by Disk Write (block IO)

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_blkio_device_usage_total{node="$node", container!="", operation="Write"}[5m])))

panels.title: Top Pods by Disk Read (block IO)

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_blkio_device_usage_total{node="$node", container!="", operation="Read"}[5m])))

panels.title: Top Pods by CPU Throttling
panels.description: Seconds throttled per second. Non-zero means the pod is hitting its CPU limit — expensive to itself, not to the node.

panels.title: Container Restarts on this Node

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (namespace, pod) (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[1h]) * on (namespace, pod) group_left () max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{node="$node"})))

panels.description: Restarts in the last hour, for pods currently scheduled here.

panels.title: Pod Cost Table (sortable)
panels.description: One row per pod on this node. Click a column header to rank by that resource.

panels.title: Storage Attribution — which volume is the disk load?
Longhorn Volume Throughput (this node)
panels.description: Per-PVC block IO for Longhorn volumes whose engine runs on this node. This is the attribution cAdvisor's blkio numbers roll up.

panels.title: Longhorn Volume Latency (this node)
panels.description: Longhorn reports latency in nanoseconds. Rising latency at flat IOPS means the replica's underlying disk is the constraint.

panels.title: NFS Client Operations
panels.description: This node acting as an NFS *client* against hoyt (192.168.50.52). This is where media traffic shows up — it is invisible to cAdvisor's block-IO panels.

panels.title: NFS RPC Retransmissions
panels.description: Non-zero means NFS requests are timing out and being resent — the classic signature of a saturated or stalled NFS server.

panels.title: Filesystem Usage (local mounts)
panels.description: NFS and PVC mounts under /var/lib/kubelet are excluded by node-exporter, so this covers local disks only.
